label: Coffee she isn't drinking
alt: Etta Ray sits alone at the kitchen table of her Bed-Stuy flat holding a cup of coffee she is not drinking, the front door open behind her onto the stairwell.
note: The film's first cut away from the laundromat: no music, no dialogue, a woman sitting still while her building moves carefully around her.

label: The signature
alt: Two uniformed officers wait in the open doorway of the Ray flat with a clipboard form while, out of focus on the landing behind them, a covered stretcher is carried down the stairs; Etta signs with a pen that has run out of ink.
note: Covers the officers' lines and Etta's. The pen running dry is the beat: she presses hard enough to leave her name in the paper.

label: Thumb over PLAY
alt: Bug Ray stands in the bedroom doorway hugging the shoebox cassette recorder, his thumb hovering over the PLAY button without pressing it.
note: Holds through the FREEZE and the SWEET JESUS title card. He never presses play here; the film cuts away instead.

label: He fixed my window
alt: A Halloween mask hanging from the fire escape; Jack Monroe waits on the stoop with a paper twist of sunflower seeds in his breast pocket and looks up as Etta Ray comes out of the door behind him.
note: Jack has just spat shells into the gutter. Etta's first line to him is a refusal of condolence, so the frame keeps both of them and the distance between them.

label: A shell on the step
alt: The coroner's van pulls away from the kerb while Bug watches from the doorway hugging the recorder and Jack, on the stoop, scrapes a sunflower seed shell off his shoe on the stone step.
note: Ends the scene: Jack has no answer to Etta's question, Etta goes inside, and he is left with a shell stuck to his shoe.

label: Behind the line she gave him
alt: In the green-tiled morgue corridor, Etta stands at the high wooden counter while a clerk in a white jacket slides a personal-effects list towards her; Jack stands two paces behind her, hands empty, staying behind the line she gave him.
note: Jack's position in this frame is the scene: he does not step up to the counter for the rest of it.

label: A pencilled thirteen
alt: Tight insert on the morgue counter: the personal-effects list, one empty glassine bag, a set of keys and the pink laundry receipt with a navy-yard address and a pencilled circled thirteen, as Etta signs the release with a dry pen.
note: The insert that starts the investigation. Jack's eye is on the receipt, not on Etta.

label: Copied onto the wrapper
alt: Close insert of Jack's hands copying the navy-yard address in pencil onto the back of an opened brown paper sunflower-seed twist, the laundry receipt and a few spilled shells beside it on the counter.
note: He asks before he takes the receipt, and copies the address rather than keeping the original.

label: A reminder on the desk
alt: Jack's shabby one-room office in late morning: he stands at the sticking sash window with his back three-quarters to camera, while in the foreground on the battered desk lie an empty glassine bag and a torn note printed in blue ballpoint capitals.
note: The desk is dressed before Pike is revealed: Jack has not turned round to look at it yet.

label: That's not evidence
alt: Lieutenant Frank Pike stands at his ease by the green filing cabinet, coat open over a rumpled suit, while Jack stands between him and the desk without touching the glassine bag and the note lying on it.
note: Covers the whole confrontation. Jack never touches the bag; Pike watches the effort it costs him.

label: Until he's gone
alt: Pike leaves Jack's office through the doorway, having closed the sticking window on his way out; Jack stands perfectly still beside his desk waiting until he is gone, hands flat on the desktop, the glassine bag and the note still untouched.
note: S05 b012 · jack-office. Jack waits until he's gone, then wraps the bag in the note and puts it in a drawer.

label: I want the book, not the woman
alt: In Vetrano's coffee shop, Corn sits alone with a slim ledger page turned face down; Jack has just sat opposite him and leaves the envelope Corn pushed across the table exactly where it is. Neither man has greeted the other.
note: S06 b001–b005 · coffee-shop · ledger. Corn does not look up; Jack does not touch the envelope.

label: Fulton Laundry
alt: Corn has turned the ledger page face up and pushes it across the marble table with one finger; Jack looks down at the line reading a laundry delivery and a delivery to Warehouse 3 without touching the page.
note: S06 b006–b010 · coffee-shop · ledger. The page is the film's map: the laundry, the date, the warehouse.

label: Five hundred dollars
alt: Corn opens the manila envelope on the marble table so Jack can see the worn bills inside and holds it down with one finger; Jack sits back, does not reach for it, and glances across at the counterman behind the espresso machine, who looks away.
note: S06 b011–b020 · coffee-shop · cash-envelope, seed-twist. Jack leaves sunflower shells on Corn's clean saucer on the way out.

label: Letting out the hem
alt: In the adjoining bedroom of the Ray flat, Etta measures her dead son's good suit against the bed and lets out the hem with a seam ripper, working carefully and dry-eyed; the manila envelope lies on the dresser where Jack has just put it.
note: S07 b001–b005 · ray-flat (bedroom) · cash-envelope. Staged in the flat's back bedroom, in the same wallpaper and palette as the plate.

label: She counts what men say is enough
alt: Etta sits at the formica table counting the bills from the open envelope one at a time, her lips moving slightly; Jack stands a few feet away watching her do it, hands in his pockets, saying nothing.
note: S07 b006–b011 · ray-flat · cash-envelope. She counts because she has learned to count what men say is enough.

label: Her face against the suit
alt: Alone at the sideboard, having put half the cash in a biscuit tin and the rest beside a funeral-home bill, Etta presses her face against her dead son's good suit with her eyes closed, now that the man who brought the money has gone.
note: S07 b012–b014 · ray-flat. Only after he has left. No sentimentality in the lighting.

label: Under the folding table
alt: Bug sits on the floor under the folding table with the shoebox recorder on his knees, one headphone cup patched with black electrical tape; Jack crouches down to talk to him at his level, keeping a careful distance.
note: S08 b001–b003 · launderette · bug-ray, jack-monroe. Camera at the boy's eye level.

label: He brought the towels back with that
alt: Under the folding table, Bug points at the pink laundry receipt spread on the linoleum with its pencilled circled thirteen and looks up at Jack as he explains; Jack follows the boy's finger with his eyes rather than reaching for the paper.
note: S08 b004–b010 · launderette · laundry-receipt. The big machine that cleans ice; the man who didn't like him seeing the cart.

label: You don't have to play it
alt: Bug holds the cassette in both hands against his chest, reluctant to put it into the recorder, frightened of what happens when it ends; Jack crouches in front of him with his open hands resting on his knees and deliberately does not reach for it.
note: S08 b011–b015 · launderette. 'I just don't want him to stop being alive when it ends.'
